title: Equality before law; equal protection of laws.
text:
Operational relevance: State agencies and public authorities administering case records must act within law and avoid arbitrary, discriminatory access or processing decisions.
Restriction: Article 14 does not itself prescribe a specific database design, retention period or encryption standard. Apply it alongside the governing statute, rules and constitutional doctrine.
RAG caution: Do not infer that all records must be publicly accessible or that every classification is unconstitutional; lawful, reasoned distinctions may be permissible.

title: Protection against compelled self-incrimination.
text:
Operational relevance: Relevant to compelled testimony and the handling/use of statements and accused-person material.
Restriction: No person accused of an offence shall be compelled to be a witness against himself or herself. Assessment of whether a particular act, statement or material is protected is fact- and precedent-dependent.
System implication: Do not design processes that falsely label compelled statements as voluntary or bypass procedural safeguards. Preserve provenance and circumstances of recording.

title: Life and personal liberty; procedure established by law.
text:
Operational relevance: Requires lawful and fair procedures affecting liberty. Privacy and dignity interests are relevant to sensitive personal data in investigative files.
Restriction: State interference must be authorised by law and satisfy applicable constitutional standards as interpreted by courts. Article 21 does not create a blanket prohibition on lawful investigation or all data processing.
Authority note: Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) v Union of India (2017) recognised privacy as a constitutionally protected right, primarily grounded in Article 21 and connected guarantees.
System implication: Use purpose limitation, least-privilege access, accountability, safeguards against wrongful disclosure, and defensible retention/deletion rules.

title: Safeguards concerning arrest and detention.
text:
Operational relevance: Case-record workflows must support recording and audit of arrest-related steps and must not frustrate access to counsel or production before a Magistrate as required by law.
Restriction: Article 22 contains specific protections and exceptions. Apply the exact text and BNSS provisions to the particular arrest/detention context.

title: Equal justice and free legal aid.
text:
Operational relevance: Supports fair access to justice and legal aid. Digital-only procedures should not practically exclude participants who need legally required assistance or accessibility accommodations.
Nature: Directive Principle of State Policy; implementation is through law and policy, not a stand-alone database specification.

title: recording of search and seizure through audio-video electronic means
text:
Rule summary: The process of conducting a search or taking possession of property/article/thing under the specified BNSS provisions, including preparation of the seizure list and witness signatures, is to be recorded through audio-video electronic means, preferably by mobile phone; the police officer must forward the recording without delay to the designated Magistrate or executive authority specified in the section.
System relevance: Preserve the original recording, metadata, transfer history, hash/check value if used, receiving acknowledgment, and access log. Ensure the system does not replace the statute’s prescribed forwarding/recording process.
Restriction/caveat: Read the exact current section and any applicable rules/orders; the requirement applies to the statutory scope, not automatically to every interaction or all evidence collection.

title: information in cognizable cases (FIR)
text:
Rule summary: Information about a cognizable offence may be given orally or by electronic communication, irrespective of where the offence occurred, subject to statutory procedure. Information given electronically is taken on record on being signed by the informant within the period specified by the section (three days). The provision also addresses recording, free copy, and escalation where the station officer refuses to record information.
System relevance: Support electronic intake, identity/provenance, timestamping, signature completion status, acknowledgment, routing, correction history and legally controlled access to FIR copies.
Restriction/caveat: Do not treat an unsigned electronic intimation as satisfying every statutory requirement. Preserve the original submission and subsequent signature/endorsement. Check statutory exceptions and exact current language.

title: procedure for investigation
text:
Rule summary: Establishes procedure following reason to suspect commission of an offence and investigation by the officer in charge, including statutory requirements that may apply to the case category.
System relevance: Preserve investigation actions, author, timing, approvals, evidence references and statutory reports as separate, traceable events.
Restriction/caveat: Do not automate legal determinations such as whether investigation is authorised or complete without accountable human/legal review.

title: police officer’s power to require attendance of witnesses
text:
Rule summary: Provides statutory authority, subject to conditions and safeguards, for requiring attendance of persons acquainted with the facts of a case.
System relevance: Track lawful notice/request, service, attendance and any applicable protected-category safeguards.
Restriction/caveat: Not an unrestricted power; read statutory conditions and exceptions in the current text.

title: examination of witnesses by police
text:
Rule summary: Governs police examination of persons acquainted with case facts and recording of statements during investigation.
System relevance: Store statement as an attributed record with date, author, language, translation/interpreter details where applicable, corrections, signature/mark where required, and a link to the underlying case.
Restriction/caveat: Do not imply that a police statement is sworn trial testimony. Its use is controlled by the BNSS and evidence law.

title: statements to police and use of such statements
text:
Rule summary: Police statements in investigation are subject to statutory restrictions on signature and use; the provision regulates their use, including specified use for contradiction in the manner allowed by evidence law.
System relevance: Label statement type accurately and enforce access/use controls. Keep it distinct from a Magistrate-recorded statement, confession, deposition or trial testimony.
Restriction/caveat: A police-recorded statement is not automatically substantive evidence merely because it is stored digitally or signed. Consult the exact text and BSA contradiction rules.

title: recording of confessions and statements by Magistrate
text:
Rule summary: Governs Magistrate recording of confessions and statements, including safeguards intended to ensure voluntariness and proper procedure.
System relevance: Capture recording authority, warnings/explanations, voluntariness-related procedural events, recording mode, signatures/attestations and custody.
Restriction/caveat: A confession must not be treated as valid simply because an audio/video file exists. Compliance with statutory safeguards and applicable evidence rules is essential.

title: diary of proceedings in investigation
text:
Rule summary: Requires the investigating officer to maintain a day-to-day record of investigation proceedings in the prescribed manner. The court may call for and use the diary only as the section allows; it is not itself substantive evidence.
System relevance: Keep case diaries logically separate from public-facing case documents, maintain edit history and enforce statutory access restrictions.
Restriction/caveat: Do not expose a case diary to parties or general users as though it were a routinely disclosable case file. Access is controlled by the statute and court directions.

title: report of police officer on completion of investigation
text:
Rule summary: Requires the police officer to forward a report to the competent Magistrate on completion of investigation and specifies information/documents and further-investigation matters to be included or addressed.
System relevance: Maintain versioned report packages, filing timestamps, receiving acknowledgment, annexures, digital signatures/certification as legally applicable and a record of supplementary reports.
Restriction/caveat: System-generated completeness checks cannot substitute for statutory review, approval or filing by the responsible officer.

title: trial and proceedings to be held in electronic mode
text:
Rule summary: Permits trials and proceedings, including specified procedural steps, to be conducted in electronic mode subject to statutory text and applicable rules.
System relevance: Supports authenticated electronic filing, secure transmission, hearing records and reliable access for participants.
Restriction/caveat: This is not permission to disregard fair-hearing rights, court rules, identity verification, record integrity or accessibility requirements.

title: primary evidence
text:
Rule summary: Defines primary evidence and includes statutory explanations relevant to electronic/digital records, including certain situations involving records created or stored in multiple files or systems.
System relevance: Preserve original native files and relevant copies/replicas, metadata, system context, provenance and custody information.
Restriction/caveat: Do not assume every digital copy is primary evidence. Apply the exact statutory clauses and facts of the record.

title: electronic or digital record
text:
Rule summary: An electronic or digital record cannot be denied admissibility solely because it is electronic/digital; subject to section 63, it has the same legal effect, validity and enforceability as other documents.
System relevance: Digital-first records can be legally relevant, but system must support authenticity, integrity, attribution and statutory evidence requirements.
Restriction/caveat: Section 61 is not a blanket guarantee of admissibility or truth; section 63 and other evidentiary rules apply.

title: special provisions as to evidence relating to electronic records
text:
Rule summary: Electronic-record evidence is subject to the special statutory provisions governing such records.
System relevance: Store records in a manner that allows the party tendering them to meet statutory proof requirements.
Restriction/caveat: Read with section 63 and current case law; do not rely only on a general assertion that the record came from a computer.

title: admissibility of electronic records
text:
Rule summary: Specifies conditions for admissibility of information in electronic records produced as computer output and a certificate framework, including prescribed particulars and responsible-person/expert elements in the statutory form/schedule.
System relevance: Capture how the output was produced, relevant devices/systems, regular-use/ordinary-course matters specified by law, integrity and certificate information. Build a workflow for the statutory certificate where required.
Restriction/caveat: A hash, audit log, digital signature or vendor attestation alone is not automatically the certificate required by section 63. Determine which person(s) and expert details are required under the current statute and applicable interpretation.

title: public documents
text:
Rule summary: Identifies categories of public documents, including records of acts of sovereign authorities, official bodies/tribunals and public officers, and public records of private documents.
System relevance: Many official police or court records may fall within public-document categories, depending on their character and custody.
Restriction/caveat: Not every file held by government is automatically a public document for every evidentiary purpose. Classify by statutory definition and document context.

title: private documents
text:
Rule summary: Documents other than those included in section 74 are private documents.
System relevance: Third-party submissions, private CCTV, medical material and private forensic records may need classification and proof accordingly.
Restriction/caveat: Classification depends on the document, not simply who uploaded or currently stores it.

title: certified copies of public documents
text:
Rule summary: Provides for certified copies of public documents in the circumstances prescribed by the section.
System relevance: Support controlled generation of certified copies, certification provenance and verification.
Restriction/caveat: Do not label an ordinary download or printout as a legally certified copy without authorised certification under applicable law.

title: proof of other official documents
text:
Rule summary: Provides rules for proof of certain official documents by certified copies or other prescribed means.
System relevance: Maintain source provenance, certification and officer authority details.
Restriction/caveat: Apply the exact category-specific conditions; digital storage does not itself satisfy certification rules.

title: scope, commencement and personal data
text:
Rule summary: Applies to digital personal data within the Act’s territorial and material scope, subject to exclusions and exemptions. The Act authorises phased commencement by separate Gazette notifications.
Operational caution: As at this corpus date, do not assume every substantive provision is already operative. Verify G.S.R. 843(E) of 13 November 2025 and later commencement notifications, amendments and the 2025 Rules against official Gazette/MeitY sources.
System relevance: Track personal data by data subject, purpose, legal basis/authority and access; build controls to activate obligations according to commencement and applicability.

title: exemptions
text:
Rule summary: Section 17 provides specified exemptions, including processing necessary for prevention, detection, investigation or prosecution of an offence or contravention of law, and processing by courts/tribunals or other specified bodies where necessary for judicial/quasi-judicial functions.
Restriction/caveat: Scope is conditional and must be read with the exact text, subsection, commencement and other applicable law. It is not a general immunity for all government processing, arbitrary disclosure, weak security or constitutionally unreasonable action.
System relevance: Record the purpose and legal authority for processing; separate investigative use from unrelated reuse; apply security and confidentiality controls under applicable instruments.

title: general obligations of Data Fiduciary
text:
Rule summary: Establishes obligations for Data Fiduciaries, including responsibility for processing, security safeguards, breach-related duties, data accuracy in relevant circumstances, erasure when purpose is no longer served subject to legal retention, grievance handling and other statutory duties, as applicable and in force.
Restriction/caveat: Must be read with section 17, other exclusions, commencement notifications and DPDP Rules. Do not assert that every duty applies to an exempt law-enforcement processing activity without legal analysis.
System relevance: Use security controls, incident response, accuracy/correction workflows and legally grounded retention schedules.

Rule summary: Rules made under the DPDP Act set operational requirements and have phased commencement specified in the rules/notification.
Operational caution: Rule commencement is staggered. Check the Gazette version, notification G.S.R. 846(E), subsequent corrigenda and official MeitY text. Do not apply future-phase deadlines as presently enforceable without checking the relevant date.

title: unauthorised acts involving computer resources
text:
Rule summary: Provides civil liability/compensation for specified unauthorised acts involving computer systems/data, such as unauthorised access, copying, introducing contaminants, damaging or disrupting systems, and related conduct described in the section.
System relevance: Supports need for access control, monitoring, incident preservation and authorisation records.
Restriction/caveat: Exact liability depends on the statutory elements, authorisation, facts and other provisions.

title: tampering with computer source documents
text:
Rule summary: Addresses knowingly or intentionally concealing, destroying or altering computer source code required by law to be kept or maintained.
System relevance: Preserve source code/configuration and required records where legally mandated; prevent unauthorised alteration and maintain change history.
Restriction/caveat: Section 65 is not a general offence provision for every alteration of any digital file. Its defined elements and scope must be met.

title: computer-related offences
text:
Rule summary: Makes specified section 43 acts criminal where done dishonestly or fraudulently, subject to statutory elements and penalty provisions.
System relevance: Unauthorised, dishonest or fraudulent interference with case systems can trigger criminal-law exposure.
Restriction/caveat: Do not describe every system error or authorised correction as a section 66 offence.

title: CERT-In
text:
Rule summary: Establishes CERT-In as the national agency for incident response and empowers it to perform functions and issue directions within the statutory framework.
System relevance: Cyber incidents affecting case systems may entail reporting, cooperation and log-production duties under valid directions.

Rule summary: Directions issued under IT Act section 70B(6). Among their requirements, covered entities must enable ICT-system logs and securely maintain them for a rolling 180 days within Indian jurisdiction; specified cyber incidents must be reported within six hours of noticing them or being brought to notice; covered entities must synchronise system clocks with prescribed time sources; and specified service providers must maintain subscriber/customer information as directed.
System relevance: Preserve security logs separately from evidentiary logs; ensure time synchronisation, retention, secure access, incident escalation and ability to furnish logs to CERT-In when lawfully required.
Restriction/caveat: The exact reporting incident list, entity scope, data fields, reporting channel and exceptions are in the official directions and later clarifications. Do not apply the 180-day rule as a universal retention rule for every case file; it concerns covered ICT logs. A security-log duty does not override case-record retention, privacy, privilege or evidentiary restrictions.

title: breach of confidentiality and privacy
text:
Rule summary: Addresses disclosure of electronic records, books, registers, correspondence, information, documents or other material obtained under powers conferred by the IT Act, in the circumstances set out in the section.
System relevance: Limit disclosure of information acquired under statutory powers and log authorised disclosure.
Restriction/caveat: Read exact statutory elements and distinguish section 72 from other confidentiality/data-protection duties.

title: disclosure of information in breach of lawful contract
text:
Rule summary: Addresses disclosure of personal information obtained while providing services under a lawful contract, with the statutory mental and harm-related elements.
System relevance: Relevant to contractors, vendors and service providers with case-data access.
Restriction/caveat: Applies only where its elements are met; contract terms, other statutory duties and government procurement/security requirements may add obligations.

Rule: Use unique user identities, least privilege, role-based access, strong authentication and periodic access review. Keep investigator, prosecutor, forensic examiner, court clerk, administrator and vendor roles distinct where their legal functions differ.
Legal basis: Security and accountability needs arise across constitutional fairness/privacy principles, DPDP where applicable, IT Act/CERT-In directions and agency rules. This is a design recommendation, not a verbatim statutory command in every listed law.

Rule: Keep an access and change audit trail that records actor, action, time, object identifier, reason/authority where required, source and outcome. Prevent silent overwrite; retain original and corrected versions.
Legal basis: Helps demonstrate provenance and investigate tampering; does not by itself establish admissibility or truth.

Rule: Record collection, sealing, transfer, receipt, analysis, copying, export and return/destruction of each evidentiary item. Bind every event to a responsible person and timestamp; preserve original media and forensic images according to approved SOPs.
Legal basis: Supports authentication and evidentiary reliability under BSA and criminal procedure; detailed chain-of-custody requirements may also arise from case law, agency SOPs and laboratory accreditation standards.

Rule: Provide a workflow for preparing, reviewing and preserving certificates required by BSA section 63, with exact statutory particulars and appropriate signatories/expert participation.
Legal basis: BSA section 63. A cryptographic hash can support integrity but is not a substitute for the statutory certificate.

Rule: Use separate classifications and permissions for FIRs, police statements, Magistrate statements/confessions, case diaries, forensic working notes, final police reports, court records and material disclosed to parties.
Legal basis: BNSS procedural distinctions and restrictions; BSA evidence/public-document rules; court orders and applicable local rules.

Rule: Collect and display only data needed for the lawful function; protect witness, victim, child, medical, biometric and location data; record any lawful disclosure and recipient.
Legal basis: Constitution/privacy principles, relevant special statutes and DPDP where applicable. Check offence-specific confidentiality laws and court orders.

Rule: Maintain a schedule by record class and legal purpose. Suspend routine deletion for litigation hold, court order, investigation, appeal or statutory retention. Do not treat CERT-In 180-day ICT-log retention as a universal case-file period.
Legal basis: Applicable criminal procedure, evidence, records-management rules, court directions, DPDP provisions when in force/applicable, CERT-In Directions for covered logs.

Rule: On suspected tampering or compromise, restrict affected access, preserve system images and logs, document response decisions, notify designated officials and assess statutory/CERT-In reporting duties. Do not alter source evidence during remediation.
Legal basis: IT Act/CERT-In requirements and agency incident-response policies.
